name: Pets
description: Pet allergens such as dander, saliva, and urine can trigger asthma symptoms. Cats and dogs are common sources. Regular cleaning, grooming, and allergen filters can help reduce exposure.

name: Pollen
description: Pollen from grasses, trees, and weeds is a major asthma trigger, especially during certain seasons. Staying indoors during high pollen days and using air purifiers may reduce symptoms.

name: Exercise
description: Exercise can cause airway narrowing in people with asthma, leading to coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath. Warming up and using prescribed inhalers can help manage symptoms.

name: Smoke
description: Smoke from tobacco, bushfires, or burning wood contains irritants that inflame the airways and worsen asthma. Avoiding smoke-filled environments is key to asthma management.

name: Cold air
description: Breathing in cold, dry air can irritate airways and trigger asthma symptoms. Wearing a scarf over your nose and mouth in winter can help warm the air before it enters the lungs.
